tei:div.tei:p:
Our God, and the God of our fathers. Thou taughtest man repentance even before the hills were formed, and the earth was made habitable;See Pesachim, lii. when the Law was still concealed with thee, and the spirit moved upon the face of the waters. When the foe seeketh to devastate the land, repentance saveth the distressed inhabitant.i. e., when the evil inclination threatens to destroy the body, repentance saves the distressed soul. It saved Adam from perdition, when he tasted the forbidden fruit;See Bereshith Rabba xxii. and it mitigated Cain’s punishment.Genesis iv. 14. Reuben, who had defiled his father’s couch, humbled himself by putting on sackcloth and by fasting.Bereshith Rabba xxiv. And though he forfeited his birth-rightGen. xlix. 4. yet for having endeavoured to restore Joseph to his father,Ibid. xxxvii. 22. he received a handsome reward.See Jalkut Hosea 451. For, from him was descended Hosea, whose father Beeri was extolled as the source of the Law, by whose virtues the tribes were brought out of the desert to the promised land, even as vile ore is sought for the gold it contains, and whose noble minded son, learned and worthy, was selected to counsel and teach repentance, saying,Hosea xiv. 2. “Israel, thy Creator is compassionate, return to him while his mercy prevaileth.” On the other hand he threatened refractory Samaria with destruction.Ibid. xiv. 1. Wise pro
phets, and even the holy Law, have been consulted as to the way by which sinners may return. The highest authorities have been appealed to.See מדרש ש״ט מזמור כ״ה. But the gracious King himself teacheth what is right and good.See Ps. xxiv. 8. His mercy may be learnt from his own mouth. Let us therefore trust in Him who is of great mercy, and let us hope he will be prevailed on by his creatures, and pardon offences; that he willingly accepteth gifts in broken vessels,i. e., that he accepts contrite hearts. for the words of supplicants are as incense to him. That is what the prophet praiseth when he sayeth,Micah vii. 18. “He pardoneth the sin of the remnant of his inheritance; who like him, teacheth sinners how to reform, is like him, propitiated by words?”—Like one who, exchanging bad money for good, hath to give the banker a premium, the penitent, by an increase of virtues and rigid abstinence, hath to make amends for his former sins, has to occupy himself with the holy Law, all the days of his life, and must not be ashamed of his repentance, for by virtue of that he may save the whole world.By setting others an example for imitation. Two prophets have in different expressions exhorted to repentance.Hosea uses the singular שובה, and Zechariah i. 2. the plural, so as to exhort the individuals as well as the community at large. “Turn, and return ye,” to your Father in heaven. The heavenly Father is easily reconciled, even as a king’s son who hath offended, easily reconcileth his father. O remember thou Israel, thy precious son, thy firstborn, thy favourite child, when he returneth to thee with sincere repentance. May his prayer be accepted as incense. O have pity on the people who displayed their readiness at the foot of Sinai,By saying: “We will do and obey.” and whom thou hast repeatedly promised thy kindness and compassion and taught how to pray in an acceptable manner, so that if they but open their hearts as wide as the ear of a needle, thine shall open to them as wide as a hall. Though therefore thou seest their iniquity, regard it not, and ascribe it to delusion. In the ordinary course of things it is the custom, that if any one offendeth his neighbour publicly, and having cooled down, trieth to appease him, he hath to ask his pardon in public. But the power of the Creator is great; he teacheth us to repent in humble silence. Therefore it behoveth us to praise his honoured name, and to appease him with pleasing words, until his spirit be poured on
us from on high, and he bring back our exiles from north and south. O may the kind One favour again the place of his sanctuary, that we may offer again on his altars; then will we render our offerings according to precept to Him who is the refuge to all the inhabitants of the earth and of the far off coasts of the sea.
